```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2026_np011_human_simple"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18091194> (open access, PMC13610530)

NP-011 is a truncated recombinant human milk fat globule-EGF factor 8 (MFG-E8)
protein that binds integrin alpha-v-beta-5 and is in development for liver
fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Lee 2026
fitted plasma NP-011 after intravenous (IV) bolus doses separately in mice,
rats and monkeys, each with a two-compartment model with first-order
elimination (Table 1), scaled the three parameter sets to a 70 kg human by
simple allometry (Table 2), and compared the projection with the single
ascending dose (SAD) part of the Phase I study (Tables 3-4, Figure 3). A
maximum-lifespan-potential (MLP) corrected projection is reported as a
supplementary sensitivity analysis. The paper therefore contributes five model
files:

| Model | Species | Basis |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `Lee_2026_np011_mouse` | mouse | population PK fit, Table 1 |
| `Lee_2026_np011_rat` | rat | population PK fit, Table 1 |
| `Lee_2026_np011_monkey` | monkey | population PK fit, Table 1 |
| `Lee_2026_np011_human_simple` | human (projected) | simple allometry, Table 2 and the supplementary NONMEM simulation control stream `SIM_SA.mod` (the paper's primary projection) |
| `Lee_2026_np011_human_mlp` | human (projected) | MLP-corrected allometry for CL and Q, Supplementary Results |

The animal models are normalised to body weight (CL and Q in L/h/kg, VC and VP
in L/kg), so their doses are entered in ug/kg. The human projections take
doses in ug. Concentrations are in ng/mL (ug/L) throughout.

# Population

* **Mice** (120; Table S1): 6-10 weeks, 23.60-38.12 g; 30 males at each of
  0.0214, 0.0854 and 0.342 mg/kg plus 30 females at 0.0854 mg/kg; single IV
  bolus; cross-sectional sampling (three mice per time point, one sample per
  mouse) from 0.083 to 24 h.
* **Rats** (12): 6-9 weeks, 228.3-368.3 g; 3 males at each of 0.00798,
  0.0426 and 0.171 mg/kg plus 3 females at 0.0426 mg/kg; serial sampling to
  24 h.
* **Monkeys** (12): 6-10 months, 2.55-4.75 kg; 3 males at 0.00534 and at
  0.0854 mg/kg single dose; 3 males and 3 females at 0.0213 mg/kg once daily
  for 14 days, sampled intensively on days 1 and 14.
* **Humans**: no human data entered the models. The SAD part of the Phase I
  study (NCT05387499) dosed 30 healthy adults (6 per cohort; mean body weight
  72.81 kg, Table S2) with 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 mg IV bolus; these data were
  used only to evaluate the projection.

Plasma NP-011 was measured by ELISA (clinical LLOQ 15.62 ng/mL). The strain
or species of the mice, rats and monkeys is not stated. The same information is
available programmatically, for example
`readModelDb("Lee_2026_np011_monkey")()$population`.

# Source trace

Structure (all files): two-compartment model, IV bolus into `central`,
`dA_c/dt = -(CL/VC + Q/VC) A_c + Q/VP A_p`, `dA_p/dt = Q/VC A_c - Q/VP A_p`,
`C = A_c/VC` (Supplementary Methods); exponential IIV `P_i = P_TV exp(eta_i)`
with a diagonal OMEGA (Supplementary Methods, Table S6); residual error on the
natural-log concentration scale (Table S6, `SIM_SA.mod` `$ERROR`), encoded as
`lnorm(expSd)`.

| Parameter | Mouse | Rat | Monkey | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, L/h/kg) | 0.363 | 0.552 | 0.0904 | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (VC, L/kg) | 0.071 | 0.0814 | 0.0475 | Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q, L/h/kg) | 0.0063 | 0.0176 | 0.00342 | Table 1 |
| `lvp` (VP, L/kg) | 0.0174 | 0.0627 | 0.103 | Table 1 |
| `etalcl` (omega^2) | 0.0133 | 0.0198 | 0.0022 | Table 1 |
| `etalvc` (omega^2) | - | - | 0.0371 | Table 1 |
| `etalvp` (omega^2) | 0.227 | - | - | Table 1 |
| `expSd` (log-scale SD) | 0.361 | 0.985 | 0.457 | Table 1 'Proportional error' |

| Parameter | Simple allometry | MLP | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, L/h) | 3.79590 | 2.58 | `SIM_SA.mod` THETA(1) (Table 2: 3.80); Supplementary Results (MLP) |
| `lvc` (VC, L) | 2.88054 | 2.88054 | `SIM_SA.mod` THETA(2) (Table 2: 2.88); MLP leaves VC unchanged |
| `lq` (Q, L/h) | 0.25010 | 0.17 | `SIM_SA.mod` THETA(4) (Table 2: 0.25); Supplementary Results (MLP) |
| `lvp` (VP, L) | 24.60960491 | 24.60960491 | `SIM_SA.mod` THETA(3) (Table 2: 24.61); MLP leaves VP unchanged |
| `etalcl` (omega^2) | 0.00216 | 0.00216 | `SIM_SA.mod` `$OMEGA` (monkey IIV; Methods 2.3) |
| `etalvc` (omega^2) | 0.0371 | 0.0371 | `SIM_SA.mod` `$OMEGA` |
| `expSd` | 0.457 | 0.457 | `SIM_SA.mod` THETA(5) (monkey residual SD) |

All human values are wrapped in `fixed()`: Methods 2.4 states that they were
obtained by allometry and fixed for simulation, not estimated.

# Animal models

Each species is simulated at its studied doses with 100 virtual animals per
dose group and sampled at the study schedule of Table S1. The 0.0213 mg/kg
monkey group receives 14 once-daily doses and is sampled on days 1 and 14.

```{r animal-helpers}
make_events <- function(doses_ugkg, times, label, first_id, n = 100L, n_doses = 1L) {
  ids <- first_id + seq_len(n) - 1L
  dose_times <- 24 * (seq_len(n_doses) - 1L)
  dose_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_times)
  dose_rows$evid <- 1L
  dose_rows$amt <- doses_ugkg
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = times)
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  out <- rbind(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$cmt <- "central"
  out$treatment <- label
  out
}

solve_species <- function(model, events, seed) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(seed)
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    readModelDb(model),
    events = dplyr::arrange(events, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)),
    keep = "treatment",
    # Tight tolerances: the mouse terminal phase falls to ~1e-10 ng/mL by
    # 24 h, where default tolerances leave small negative values.
    atol = 1e-14, rtol = 1e-10
  )
  as.data.frame(sim)
}

rodent_times <- c(0, 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 24)
monkey_times <- c(0, 0.083, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 24)
# Day-1 trough at 23.99 h so that it precedes the 24-h dose.
monkey_mad_times <- c(setdiff(monkey_times, 24), 23.99, 312 + monkey_times)

mouse_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(21.4, rodent_times, "Mouse 21.4 ug/kg", 1L),
  make_events(85.4, rodent_times, "Mouse 85.4 ug/kg", 101L),
  make_events(342, rodent_times, "Mouse 342 ug/kg", 201L)
)
rat_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(7.98, rodent_times, "Rat 7.98 ug/kg", 1L),
  make_events(42.6, rodent_times, "Rat 42.6 ug/kg", 101L),
  make_events(171, rodent_times, "Rat 171 ug/kg", 201L)
)
monkey_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(5.34, monkey_times, "Monkey 5.34 ug/kg", 1L),
  make_events(21.3, monkey_mad_times, "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg QD x14", 101L, n_doses = 14L),
  make_events(85.4, monkey_times, "Monkey 85.4 ug/kg", 201L)
)

animal_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_species("Lee_2026_np011_mouse", mouse_ev, 2026L),
  solve_species("Lee_2026_np011_rat", rat_ev, 2027L),
  solve_species("Lee_2026_np011_monkey", monkey_ev, 2028L)
)
```

```{r animal-vpc, fig.height = 7}
vpc <- animal_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after IV bolus (h)", y = "Plasma NP-011 (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated median and 90% prediction interval (day 1)",
    caption = "Compare with the visual predictive checks of Figures S5-S7 of Lee 2026."
  )
```

## PKNCA against the observed NCA (Tables S3-S5)

Tables S3-S5 report non-compartmental parameters of the observed data (Phoenix
WinNonlin, IV bolus, with the initial concentration C0 back-extrapolated). The
simulated profiles are analysed with PKNCA on the study schedule: the
concentration at time 0 is the post-bolus concentration (the quantity C0
back-extrapolation estimates), Cmax is taken from the first post-dose sample
at 0.083 h, as it was in the observed data, and AUCinf uses the observed
terminal phase.

```{r animal-nca}
animal_conc <- animal_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
animal_dose <- animal_sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::bind_rows(mouse_ev, rat_ev, monkey_ev) |>
      dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
      dplyr::distinct(treatment, amt),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0)

single <- setdiff(unique(animal_conc$treatment), "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg QD x14")
intervals <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(treatment = single, start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE),
  data.frame(treatment = single, start = 0.083, end = 24, cmax = TRUE),
  data.frame(treatment = "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg QD x14", start = c(0, 312), end = c(23.99, 336), auclast = TRUE),
  data.frame(treatment = "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg QD x14", start = c(0.083, 312.083), end = c(23.99, 336), cmax = TRUE)
)
intervals[is.na(intervals)] <- FALSE

animal_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(animal_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(animal_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = intervals
))

sim_long <- as.data.frame(animal_nca$result) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = dplyr::case_when(
      treatment == "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg QD x14" & start >= 312 ~ "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg day 14",
      treatment == "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg QD x14" ~ "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg day 1",
      TRUE ~ treatment
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

# Tables S3-S5, arithmetic means (ug/L = ng/mL; ug*h/L = ng*h/mL). Where a
# dose group was split by sex, the reference is the mean of the male and
# female group means (equal group sizes).
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~auclast,
  "Mouse 21.4 ug/kg", 410, 64.7, NA,
  "Mouse 85.4 ug/kg", (1668 + 1654) / 2, (287 + 195) / 2, NA,
  "Mouse 342 ug/kg", 9212, 1353, NA,
  "Rat 7.98 ug/kg", 155, 18.8, NA,
  "Rat 42.6 ug/kg", (693 + 995) / 2, (63 + 78.9) / 2, NA,
  "Rat 171 ug/kg", 1449, 271, NA,
  "Monkey 5.34 ug/kg", 126, 61, NA,
  "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg day 1", (444 + 408) / 2, NA, (203 + 214) / 2,
  "Monkey 21.3 ug/kg day 14", (477 + 311) / 2, NA, (253 + 215) / 2,
  "Monkey 85.4 ug/kg", 2055, 1166, NA
)

cmp_animal <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_long,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "group",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_animal,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median of 100 animals per group) vs. observed NCA means",
    "(Tables S3-S5). * differs by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

```{r animal-checks}
auc_ratio <- sim_long |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    published_nca |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(c(aucinf.obs, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "obs") |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(obs)),
    by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = sim / obs)
# AUC is set by CL alone; a mis-transcribed CL or a dose-unit slip moves the
# typical ratio far beyond this band.
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_ratio) == 10L,
  abs(log(median(auc_ratio$ratio))) < log(1.25)
)
```

AUCinf, which is set by CL alone, is within about 25% of the observed mean in
nine of the ten groups (median simulated-to-observed ratio
`r signif(median(auc_ratio$ratio), 2)`). The rat model, which the paper notes
has strong parameter correlations (CL-VC 0.958) and a large residual SD
(0.985), runs below the lowest-dose AUC (observed 18.8 ng*h/mL against a
dose/CL of 14.5) and above the highest, because the rat NCA clearance itself
varies from 0.44 to 0.71 L/h/kg across groups (Table S4) while the model has
one CL. The mouse 0.342 mg/kg group has the highest dose-normalised AUC of the
mouse groups (3.96 against 2.3-3.4, Table S3), and the monkey 0.0854 mg/kg
group the highest of the monkey groups (13.7, Table S5), so a single linear
CL under-predicts both by 20-30%. In the repeated-dose monkey group the
simulated day-14 AUC and Cmax equal day 1, in line with the paper's
observation that day-14 dose-normalised AUC was comparable to day 1.

The Cmax rows differ more, and the difference is in the reference rather than
the model. The NCA mean Cmax of the rodent groups (for example 410 ng/mL in
mice and 155 ng/mL in rats at the lowest doses) exceeds the model's own
time-zero concentration, dose/VC (301 and 98 ng/mL), whereas the observed
medians at 0.083 h plotted in the paper's visual predictive checks (Figures S5
and S6, read approximately) are about 200 and 60 ng/mL, close to the simulated
medians of 195 and 55 ng/mL. The NCA Cmax summarises the observed data
differently from the profiles the models were fitted to (mouse sampling was
cross-sectional, three animals per time point), so the Cmax comparison is
shown for completeness and is not asserted on. The simulated profiles in the
figure above follow the shapes of Figures S5-S7, including the slow, low
terminal phase of the monkey profiles.

# Human projection by simple allometry

## Typical values (Table 2, Table 3, Table S10)

For the typical 70 kg adult, AUCinf = dose/CL, Cmax = dose/VC (the IV bolus
concentration at time 0, which is how `SIM_SA.mod` defines CMAX) and the
hybrid half-lives follow from Equation 6.

```{r human-typical}
hybrid_half_lives <- function(cl, vc, q, vp) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  disc <- sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)
  c(alpha = log(2) / ((s + disc) / 2), beta = log(2) / ((s - disc) / 2))
}

typical <- function(model) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(model))$theta
  exp(p[c("lcl", "lvc", "lq", "lvp")])
}
tv_sa <- typical("Lee_2026_np011_human_simple")
doses_ug <- c(250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000)
hl_sa <- hybrid_half_lives(tv_sa[["lcl"]], tv_sa[["lvc"]], tv_sa[["lq"]], tv_sa[["lvp"]])

typ_tab <- data.frame(
  dose_mg = doses_ug / 1000,
  auc_typ = doses_ug / tv_sa[["lcl"]],
  auc_s10 = c(65.9, 131.7, 263.4, 526.9, 1053.8),
  cmax_typ = doses_ug / tv_sa[["lvc"]],
  cmax_s10 = c(86.8, 173.6, 347.2, 694.3, 1388.6)
)
typ_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(auc_typ, cmax_typ), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose_mg,
    "AUCinf = dose/CL (ng*h/mL)" = auc_typ,
    "Table S10 fixed-effects AUCinf" = auc_s10,
    "Cmax = dose/VC (ng/mL)" = cmax_typ,
    "Table S10 fixed-effects Cmax" = cmax_s10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value exposure vs. the fixed-effects simulation of Table S10 Panel C.")
signif(hl_sa, 4)

# Closed-form identities of the typical parameters: the only differences
# are the rounding of the printed values.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(typ_tab$auc_typ / typ_tab$auc_s10 - 1) < 0.005),
  all(abs(typ_tab$cmax_typ / typ_tab$cmax_s10 - 1) < 0.005),
  abs(hl_sa[["alpha"]] / 0.49 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(hl_sa[["beta"]] / 72.73 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The typical AUCinf and Cmax match the fixed-effects predictions of Table S10
Panel C to within the printed rounding, and the typical half-lives (0.49 h and
72.7 h) match the values given in the Table S10 notes.

## Variability-based simulation (Table 3)

As in the paper, 200 virtual adults per dose group are simulated with the
monkey IIV on CL and VC. The paper's intervals exclude residual error, so the
error-free prediction `Cc` is summarised.

```{r human-sim}
human_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48,
  seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), 72, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504
)))
human_dose_group <- function(i, n = 200L) {
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n + seq_len(n)
  dose_rows <- data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = doses_ug[i])
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = human_times)
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  out <- rbind(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$cmt <- "central"
  out$dose_mg <- doses_ug[i] / 1000
  out
}
hum_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_ug), human_dose_group)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(12345)
hum_sa <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  readModelDb("Lee_2026_np011_human_simple"),
  events = hum_ev, keep = "dose_mg"
))

hum_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    hum_sa |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_mg),
    Cc ~ time | dose_mg + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    hum_ev |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_mg),
    amt ~ time | dose_mg + id,
    route = "intravascular"
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

table3 <- data.frame(
  dose_mg = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4),
  aucinf.obs = c(66, 132, 264, 526, 1053),
  cmax = c(87, 173, 345, 695, 1391),
  half.life = c(72.73, 72.74, 72.74, 72.73, 72.73)
)
cmp_human <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = hum_nca,
  reference = table3,
  by = "dose_mg",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_human, caption = "Simulated (median of 200 per dose) vs. Table 3 medians.")
```

```{r human-checks}
hum_res <- as.data.frame(hum_nca$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_mg, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = median(PPORRES),
    lo = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    hi = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = c(med, lo, hi)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(table3, by = "dose_mg") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (med_aucinf.obs / aucinf.obs - 1),
    cmax_pct = 100 * (med_cmax / cmax - 1)
  )
hum_res |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    dose_mg,
    auc_pi = sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", lo_aucinf.obs, hi_aucinf.obs),
    cmax_pi = sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", lo_cmax, hi_cmax)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    data.frame(
      dose_mg = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4),
      auc_pi_t3 = c("61-71", "122-142", "244-285", "489-569", "976-1139"),
      cmax_pi_t3 = c("64-118", "126-236", "249-475", "507-949", "1011-1886")
    ),
    by = "dose_mg"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose_mg,
    "Simulated 90% PI AUCinf" = auc_pi,
    "Table 3 90% PI AUCinf" = auc_pi_t3,
    "Simulated 90% PI Cmax" = cmax_pi,
    "Table 3 90% PI Cmax" = cmax_pi_t3
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "90% prediction intervals (5th-95th percentiles) vs. Table 3.")

# Medians over a random cohort: assert on the centre across the five doses.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(hum_res$auc_pct)) < 5,
  abs(median(hum_res$cmax_pct)) < 5
)
```

The simulated medians reproduce Table 3. AUCinf from PKNCA includes the
extrapolated terminal phase (t1/2,beta about 72.7 h), and its 90% interval is
narrow because only the small monkey IIV on CL (omega^2 0.00216) enters it;
the Cmax interval reflects the IIV on VC.

## Comparison with the Phase I SAD data (Figure 3, Table 4)

The supplementary file `aggregate_Figure3_SA_profile.csv` provides the observed
5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the Phase I SAD concentrations at each
nominal time point; they are overlaid on the simulated interval below.

```{r figure3, fig.height = 7}
# Observed Phase I SAD percentiles, aggregate_Figure3_SA_profile.csv (Lee 2026
# supplementary file), rows with observations only.
obs_fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_mg, ~time, ~n, ~obs_p50, ~obs_p5, ~obs_p95,
  0.25, 0.083, 6, 50.525, 27.297, 83.49,
  0.25, 0.25, 6, 36.797, 23.639, 57.792,

ggplot() +

  geom_ribbon(data = obs_fig3, aes(time, ymin = obs_p5, ymax = obs_p95), fill = "#7CAE00", alpha = 0.25) +

  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after IV bolus (h)", y = "Plasma NP-011 (ng/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 3 of Lee 2026: red, simulated median and 5th-95th percentile",
      "(simple allometry); green, observed Phase I median (points) and 5th-95th percentile."
    )
  )
```

```{r table4}
# Table 4 of Lee 2026: observed Phase I medians and the published P/O ratios.
table4 <- data.frame(
  dose_mg = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4),
  obs_auc = c(34, 74, 163, 286, 595),
  po_auc_paper = c(1.96, 1.78, 1.62, 1.84, 1.77),
  obs_cmax = c(61, 130, 259, 505, 940),
  po_cmax_paper = c(1.42, 1.33, 1.33, 1.38, 1.48)
)
t4 <- hum_res |>
  dplyr::select(dose_mg, med_aucinf.obs, med_cmax) |>
  dplyr::left_join(table4, by = "dose_mg") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    po_auc = med_aucinf.obs / obs_auc,
    po_cmax = med_cmax / obs_cmax
  )
t4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    dose_mg, obs_auc,
    po_auc = round(po_auc, 2), po_auc_paper,
    obs_cmax,
    po_cmax = round(po_cmax, 2), po_cmax_paper
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose_mg,
    "Observed AUCinf median" = obs_auc,
    "P/O AUCinf (simulated)" = po_auc,
    "P/O AUCinf (Table 4)" = po_auc_paper,
    "Observed Cmax median" = obs_cmax,
    "P/O Cmax (simulated)" = po_cmax,
    "P/O Cmax (Table 4)" = po_cmax_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Predicted-to-observed ratios, simulated vs. Table 4.")

afe <- function(p, o) 10^mean(log10(p / o))
c(AFE_AUCinf = afe(t4$med_aucinf.obs, t4$obs_auc), AFE_Cmax = afe(t4$med_cmax, t4$obs_cmax))
```

The projection over-predicts the observed Phase I exposure as the paper
reports: AUCinf by about 1.6- to 2.0-fold and Cmax by about 1.3- to 1.5-fold,
with an average fold error near the published 1.79 (AUCinf) and 1.39 (Cmax).
The observed Phase I concentrations fall faster than the projection between
0.5 and 2 h; the paper notes that only 17.1% of the observed concentrations
lie inside the simulated 5th-95th percentile interval.

# Human projection with the MLP correction

```{r human-mlp}
tv_mlp <- typical("Lee_2026_np011_human_mlp")
hl_mlp <- hybrid_half_lives(tv_mlp[["lcl"]], tv_mlp[["lvc"]], tv_mlp[["lq"]], tv_mlp[["lvp"]])
mlp_tab <- data.frame(
  dose_mg = doses_ug / 1000,
  auc_typ = signif(doses_ug / tv_mlp[["lcl"]], 4),
  auc_s12 = c(97, 194, 389, 775, 1552),
  cmax_typ = signif(doses_ug / tv_mlp[["lvc"]], 4),
  cmax_s12 = c(87, 173, 345, 695, 1391)
)
mlp_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose_mg,
    "AUCinf = dose/CL (ng*h/mL)" = auc_typ,
    "Table S12 median AUCinf" = auc_s12,
    "Cmax = dose/VC (ng/mL)" = cmax_typ,
    "Table S12 median Cmax" = cmax_s12
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "MLP projection, typical values vs. Table S12 medians.")
signif(hl_mlp, 4)

stopifnot(
  all(abs(mlp_tab$auc_typ / mlp_tab$auc_s12 - 1) < 0.01),
  abs(hl_mlp[["alpha"]] / 0.73 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(hl_mlp[["beta"]] / 107.3 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The MLP correction lowers CL and Q by the same factor (about 0.68), so
AUCinf rises by 1.47-fold, Cmax is unchanged, and the terminal half-life
lengthens to about 107 h, as in Table S12 and the Supplementary Results. With
Q printed to two significant figures (0.17 L/h) the typical t1/2,beta is
`r signif(hl_mlp[["beta"]], 4)` h against the published median of 107.3 h.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** The DV was the natural-log concentration and the
  residual model `Y = log(F) + W * EPS(1)` with `W = sqrt(THETA(5)^2 +
  THETA(6)^2 / IPRED^2)` (`SIM_SA.mod`); Table 1 calls THETA(5) the
  "proportional error" and Table S6 "proportional (log scale)". It is encoded
  as `lnorm(expSd)` with the Table 1 value as the log-scale SD. The additive
  component THETA(6) was fixed to a negligible value (1e-5 in `SIM_SA.mod`,
  "Fixed to 0" in Table 1) and is omitted.
* **Human variability.** The paper assumes the human IIV equals the monkey
  IIV (Methods 2.3). The human files use the `SIM_SA.mod` OMEGA values
  (0.00216 on CL, 0.0371 on VC); Table 1 prints the monkey CL value rounded to
  0.0022, which is what the monkey file carries. The human residual SD (0.457)
  is the monkey value carried in `SIM_SA.mod`; the paper's prediction
  intervals exclude it, so the simulations above summarise the error-free
  `Cc`.
* **Human structural values.** The simple-allometry file uses the unrounded
  `SIM_SA.mod` THETAs, which round to Table 2. The MLP file uses CL 2.58 L/h
  and Q 0.17 L/h as printed in the Supplementary Results (the MLP regression
  inputs, such as the body weights used for each species, are not reported)
  and the simple-allometry VC and VP, which the MLP method leaves unchanged.
* **No weight covariate.** The allometric coefficients and exponents are in
  Table S10, but the human files encode only the 70 kg prediction that the
  paper simulated; there is no body-weight term.
* **Animal dosing units.** The animal fits used body-weight-normalised doses
  (ug/kg) and parameters (Supplementary Methods), so the animal files take
  doses in ug/kg and have no weight covariate.
* **Animal NCA references.** Tables S3-S5 report means of the observed NCA by
  dose group (and by sex in one group per species); for the sex-split groups
  the reference is the mean of the two group means. The simulated values are
  medians. The observed NCA terminal half-lives (0.13-4 h) describe the
  quantifiable samples only and are not compared: the fitted models have a
  slow, low-amplitude peripheral phase.
* **Species details.** The strain of the mice and rats and the monkey species
  are not stated in the paper.
